_comment: EIP-1153 (transient storage) support per chain id. Consumed by script/BackendGuard.sol.
_rules: true  -> deploy the default build (forge build)
false -> deploy the legacy build (FOUNDRY_PROFILE=legacy forge build)
A chain absent from this file will REVERT the deploy. That is intentional.
Re-verify before every deploy: chains gain Cancun support over time, and an entry
written months ago is a claim about a network that may have upgraded since.
_verification_method: Every entry below was verified EMPIRICALLY against the live chain, not from documentation.
Neither Plasma nor Stable documents its hardfork, so reading docs would have meant guessing.
Probe: a read-only eth_call executing initcode 0x600060005D60006000F3
(PUSH1 0, PUSH1 0, TSTORE, PUSH1 0, PUSH1 0, RETURN).
Control: the same initcode with SSTORE (0x55) in place of TSTORE (0x5D), valid on every EVM,
to prove the endpoint accepts the call shape at all.
A chain lacking EIP-1153 treats 0x5D as an invalid opcode and the call fails.
Verified 2026-09-09. Re-run before deploying.
2026-09-17: 4663 (Robinhood Chain) added. It was MISSING although the live Vault there is the
cancun build: the classification was never consulted because no core script called BackendGuard
until BaseScript.setUp() started doing so the same day. Probed 2026-09-18 04:0x UTC against
rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com: TSTORE initcode returned 0x (success); SSTORE control returned 0x.
2026-09-09 addendum: chains 1, 8453 and 56 probed across multiple independent endpoints.
Probing several endpoints per chain is deliberate - a single endpoint can be wrong. eth.merkle.io
returned TSTORE failure for Ethereum mainnet while its SSTORE control passed; every other source disagrees.
2026-09-18 05:51-05:55 UTC: ALL FIFTEEN target chains re-probed by packages/sdk/scripts/certify-chains.mjs
(docs/chain-certification.md). Probe: creation eth_call of 0x600160005d60005c60005260206000f3
(PUSH1 1, PUSH1 0, TSTORE, PUSH1 0, TLOAD, PUSH1 0, MSTORE, PUSH1 32, PUSH1 0, RETURN) which must
RETURN exactly 1 - it executes TLOAD as well as TSTORE, and an endpoint answering 0x for anything
cannot pass. Control: the same shape with SSTORE/SLOAD. Asked of EVERY SDK endpoint per chain;
conclusive = both the probe and the control were executed. Zero endpoints anywhere reported
TSTORE failing; the only non-answers were gateways refusing creation eth_call (thirdweb 429s under
load, flashbots has no eth_call, zan.top rejects the shape, monad-testnet.drpc.org rejects the shape).
zkEVM caveat (Linea, X Layer): eth_call runs on the node's EVM, not the prover; BackendGuard on
chain at deploy time remains the authoritative check.
_not_yet_classified: 998 (HyperEVM testnet): the endpoint probed did not respond. Unreachable is NOT the same as
failing, but it is unverified either way, so it stays out.
The absence makes a deploy to that chain fail closed until someone probes it.
